# AutoPromote flagship film: The Small Boat

**Private creative reset, 8 October 2026.** The podcast, quota, interview, and UI montage edit is rejected. This treatment supersedes that sequence. The film must stand on one visual idea and sound, with AutoPromote's identity at the opening and the final movie itself as the product proof. No feature narration or unsupported product claim.

## The story

An ordinary folded paper boat sits on a worktable. A drop of water spreads across the paper. The table seems to become an ocean; the little boat is suddenly too fragile for the scale of its world. Its creases become structure, the folded sail becomes canvas, the hull becomes timber, and the camera carries us into a real yacht moving through the same wave. The opening identity is the ignition of that world, not an unrelated bumper.

Why should a stranger care? They understand a tiny vessel confronted by an overwhelming sea, and they want to see whether it survives. The paper-to-yacht change is the earned answer. The ordinary starting material and impossible transformation imply what made the film without explaining a tool list.

## Intended cut (approximately 18–24 seconds, pending source review)

| Time | Visual / sound | Story function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–5s | Black. A restrained light reveals one edge of a physical AutoPromote identity. Separate material layers meet under a moving camera. Bass and mechanical texture rise; the mark locks on an impact and holds clearly. | Establish authorship and promise a crafted cinematic world. The ident must look like illuminated depth and motion, never a glowing 2D word. |
| 5–8s | The departing highlight matches a line of light across folded paper on a dark worktable. One boat, one drop, a slight camera push. Room tone narrows to a low pulse. | Give the viewer an object and an impending threat. Withhold the ocean and yacht. |
| 8–13s | Water overtakes the surface. The paper boat remains readable long enough to recognize its folds; its sail/mast grows from the crease and its hull changes material as the camera moves through the wave. Sound rises with the water and structural change. | Make the transition the main creative event. Every new element must have visible continuity with the paper shape. |
| 13–18s | The vessel has become a photographic yacht moving through the same sea. Give its full hull and sail room in frame. Music opens; water and wind continue across the seam. | Pay off the threat and prove the transformation was one continuous world. |
| 18–21s | Hold on the yacht's forward motion and a clean final horizon, then cut on sound to black. | Let the result breathe. Avoid an extra unrelated shot or explanatory card. |

No beginning shot should reveal the yacht before the paper has earned it. No podcast, quota screenshot, app UI, stock montage, camera-switch effect, fake human identity, or decorative particles. If the current VACE take shows a detached mast, disguises the hull change with spray, or cuts abruptly from desk to sea, reject the take. If the ident reads as a flat fade or tiny logo, reject the ident.

## Asset and editorial gates

1. Review the current bounded NVIDIA VACE take frame by frame and at normal speed. Save its artifact hash, request/model/settings, contact sheet and seam evidence. Only accepted footage enters the existing Content Factory asset library.
2. Review five NVIDIA Blender ident frames before a complete 5-second render. Preserve editable camera, material, layer, light and sound-cue parameters. Revise geometry/material or camera if the mark lacks physical depth.
3. Capture or generate a short opening bridge from the ident highlight to the paper worktable only if the paper shot needs it. It must carry the same screen direction and light, not introduce another story.
4. Build sound around the emotional change: near silence → texture and water pressure → structural rise → impact → expansive wind/sea/music. Verify the impact against the logo lock and the transformation against the first full-yacht frame.
5. Assemble with the existing Factory → Director → renderer contracts, retain CPU final-encode fallback, and watch/listen to the full private render. A technical pass is not creative acceptance.

The prior 51-second founder cut and derivatives remain private rejected prototypes. Do not publish or call this treatment a delivered film until all visual and audio gates pass.

Founder steering: one sailor on the yacht; action must advance the story, not serve as background lifestyle footage.
